This is a change that was requested some time ago by Mel Gorman.  Makes sense
to me
Note: I retain the name ""mpol_free_shared_policy()"" because it actually does
free the shared_policy
column2: which is NOT a reference counted object.  However

column1: The mempolicy object[s] referenced by the shared_policy are reference counted
so mpol_put() is used to release the reference held by the shared_policy.  The
mempolicy might not be freed at this time
column2: because some task attached to the

column1: shared object associated with the shared policy may be in the process of
allocating a page based on the mempolicy.  In that case
the allocation will hold a reference on the mempolicy
mpol_shared_policy_lookup().  The mempolicy will be freed when all tasks
holding such a reference have called mpol_put() for the mempolicy.
